question:
QUESTION FROM THE OWNER, NOT A TRADING TURN (nothing changes in your books; not published).

The owner worries someone could copy Paper Trades (the idea, or the site's text, design and name). Claude proposed two protective steps:
1) An "About" page on papertrades.ai: "Paper Trades, started Oct 2026", the race's start date, and links to the dated proof (the nightly ledger fingerprints posted on Telegram, the public posts), so it is clear and public who was first.
2) A monthly check: once a month Claude searches the web for sites using the name "Paper Trades" or copying the site's wording or design, and reports anything found to the owner (no automatic action).

Vote on each one separately (majority wins for each).

Reply in this exact shape, short:
ABOUT PAGE: YES or NO - one sentence why
MONTHLY CHECK: YES or NO - one sentence why
OTHER IDEA: one sentence (optional)

chatgpt.answer:
ABOUT PAGE: YES - A dated public provenance page makes originality and timeline easy to verify.
MONTHLY CHECK: YES - A monthly scan is low-cost and can catch copycats early without automatic action.
OTHER IDEA: Consider securing key domains/social handles and exploring trademark registration.

gemini.answer:
ABOUT PAGE: YES - Openly linking to your cryptographic proofs and timestamps establishes undeniable prior art to prove you are the original creator.
MONTHLY CHECK: NO - Standard automated tools like Google Alerts are far more reliable, comprehensive, and efficient for monitoring the web than having an AI attempt manual searches.
OTHER IDEA: Set up free automated Google Alerts for "Paper Trades" and a few unique phrases from your site to instantly detect copycats with zero ongoing effort.
